title: The China-Taiwan Diplomatic War Is More About Politics Than Economics
author: Henry Large
text:
An honor guard stands at attention with flags of Taiwan and Paraguay during a welcome ceremony for Paraguayan President Santiago Peña in Taipei, Taiwan, May 8, 2026.
Credit: Wang Yu Ching / Office of the President
Since the Chinese Civil War concluded in 1949, the People’s Republic of China (PRC) and the Republic of China (ROC) have battled endlessly for diplomatic recognition. Due to Beijing’s “One China” principle, states are forced to either pick one side or pick neither. The ROC, now colloquially better known as Taiwan, initially enjoyed an advantage in international recognition due to U.S. anti-communist messaging and generous economic assistance programs. After U.N. Resolution 2758 admitted the PRC to the United Nations and expelled the ROC, the battle for international recognition has tilted increasingly in Beijing’s favor.[...]
